assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Atomic number
items.clue: The number of protons in an atom of an element.

items.label: Positive ion
items.clue: An atom that has lost one or more outer electrons.

items.label: Mass number
items.clue: The total number of protons and neutrons in an atom.

items.label: Scientific model
items.clue: A description or picture used to explain observations.

questions.stem: Which of these is closest to the radius of a typical atom?

options.text: About 1 x 10^-10 m, a ten-billionth of a metre
About 1 x 10^-15 m, the size of a nucleus
About 1 x 10^-6 m, a thousandth of a mm
About 1 x 10^-3 m, the width of a pin head

questions.explanation: The specification gives the radius of an atom as about 1 x 10^-10 metres.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the basic structure of an atom?

options.text: A positive nucleus of protons and electrons, with neutrons outside
A positive nucleus of protons and neutrons, surrounded by electrons
A negative nucleus of protons and neutrons, with electrons outside it
A core of neutrons only, with protons and electrons around it

questions.explanation: This is the structure given in the specification: a positively charged nucleus composed of protons and neutrons, surrounded by negatively charged electrons.

questions.stem: How does the radius of a nucleus compare with the radius of the atom?

options.text: It is about 1/10 of the atom's radius, as pictured
It is roughly 1/100 of the atom's radius in all atoms
It is less than 1/10 000 of the atom's radius
It is about half of the atom's whole radius

questions.explanation: The specification states that the radius of a nucleus is less than 1/10 000 of the radius of an atom.

questions.stem: Where is nearly all of the mass of an atom found?

options.text: In the electrons, because there are so many of them
Spread out evenly throughout the atom's volume
In the nucleus, which holds the protons only
In the nucleus, in the protons and neutrons

questions.explanation: Most of the mass of an atom is concentrated in the nucleus.

questions.stem: An electron in an atom absorbs electromagnetic radiation. What happens to that electron?

options.text: It moves closer to the nucleus, to a lower energy level
It moves further from the nucleus, to a higher energy level
It escapes the atom, leaving behind a positive ion
It stays where it is but orbits a little quicker

questions.explanation: Absorption of electromagnetic radiation moves an electron further from the nucleus, to a higher energy level.

questions.stem: An atom emits electromagnetic radiation. What has one of its electrons done?

options.text: Moved further from the nucleus, to a higher energy level
Left the atom, carrying the energy away with it
Moved closer to the nucleus, to a lower energy level
Settled at a new distance of its own choosing

questions.explanation: Emission of electromagnetic radiation accompanies an electron moving closer to the nucleus, to a lower energy level.
